titel: Set up company sign-in with Microsoft Entra ID
kurz: Users sign in on the online site with their company account (“Sign in with company account”) – without a password of their own and without a second factor in the AMW; the company's identity provider handles both. Only people an admin created in the AMW get in.
brauchst: The online site and online storage, set up, and the site's address under Settings › Online site.
An account in Microsoft Entra ID that may register apps (e.g. “Application Administrator”).
To assign groups: Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher (otherwise assign individual users).
The Workbench on the PC and a system-admin sign-in to the online site (for the secret).

schritte.titel: Read the address for the provider
schritte.text: On the PC: Settings › Users of the online site › Company sign-in. It shows the **Redirect URI**, e.g. `https://amw.example.com/sso.php`. You need it exactly like that.

In the Microsoft Entra admin center (entra.microsoft.com) › Applications › **App registrations** › **New registration**. Name: e.g. “AMW Workbench”. Supported account types: **Accounts in this organizational directory only**. Redirect URI: platform **Web**, the address from step 1. › Register.
On the app's **Overview** page: **Application (client) ID** and **Directory (tenant) ID**.
› API permissions › Add a permission › Microsoft Graph › Delegated permissions: **openid**, **profile**, **email**. Then “Grant admin consent” so nobody is asked individually.
› Token configuration › Add optional claim › token type **ID** › **email**. Without this step the AMW uses the sign-in name (UPN) – fine if it equals the email.

› Certificates & secrets. Either **Client secrets** › New client secret › pick an expiry › copy the **Value** right away (shown only once; not the “Secret ID”). Or **Certificates** › Upload certificate (public part only, .cer/.pem) – the safer choice; you need certificate and private key in step 8.

Enterprise applications › “AMW Workbench” › Properties › **Assignment required?** **Yes** › Save. Then › **Users and groups** › Add user/group › e.g. the group “AMW team”. Anyone not assigned is turned away by Microsoft already.

schritte.titel: Enter the secret on the online site
schritte.text: Sign in on the online site as a system admin and open `…/sso.php?einrichten` (on the PC, the link “Enter it on the online site” goes there). Paste the secret – or certificate and private key as PEM – › Save. It goes into the configuration file at the web host outside the web folder and is never shown again.

Settings › Users of the online site › Company sign-in: **Issuer** `https://login.microsoftonline.com/<Directory ID>/v2.0`, **Application (client) ID**, tick “Show the button” › Save. Or on the command line: `amw web sso --aussteller https://login.microsoftonline.com/<Directory ID>/v2.0 --client-id <Application ID> --an`.
For each person in the list above: create the name, **email** as in the company account, role and projects › Save. No activation code is needed for company sign-in.
Open the online site in a private window › **Sign in with company account**. The first time, the AMW binds the company account to the user; you get a message (also as push).

werte: shown on the PC under Company sign-in, ends in `/sso.php`
value of the client secret – or certificate + private key (PEM)
email address of the company account
fehler: “Show the button” is off on the PC, or the secret is still missing on the online site. On the PC, “Secret at the web host” says what is missing.
Microsoft reports AADSTS50011 (reply URL does not match)
The redirect URI in the app differs. Enter exactly the address from the PC, platform “Web” (not “Single-page application”).
The person is not assigned to the app (step 7).
Secret wrong, expired, or the “Secret ID” entered instead of the value. Create a new one and replace it on the online site.
The message says “common/organizations” does not work
Enter the directory ID instead of `common`. Only then is it certain that only your company's accounts get in.
“Your company account (…) is not enabled here”
There is no AMW user with this email, or the user is blocked. Enter the shown address for the user.
Signed in, but role or projects are missing. Assign them on the PC, then reload the page.
“Sign-in took too long or came from another browser”
More than 10 minutes between button and return, or cookies are blocked. Press the button again.
danach: When the secret expires (Microsoft: 24 months at most), create a new one and replace it on `sso.php?einrichten` – before, or nobody gets in by company account.
A new email for a user releases the binding to the previous company account; so does “Reset access”. Their sessions end at once.
Blocking in the AMW works immediately, even while the company account stays valid.
The existing sign-in from the site's configuration (password + second factor) always stays – as a fallback if the identity provider is down.
fragen: Does this work with Keycloak, Google or another provider?

Yes, with any OpenID Connect provider. The issuer is the address under which `/.well-known/openid-configuration` lives, e.g. `https://login.company.com/realms/company` for Keycloak. When you enter the secret on the online site, the AMW checks that the provider is reachable and reports exactly this issuer.
Why no second factor in the AMW?
The company's identity provider requires it (e.g. through a Conditional Access policy). A second one in the AMW would be twice.
What does the AMW check on return?
The token signature with the provider's key, issuer, audience (the client ID), expiry and a random value of this one sign-in. The exchange uses PKCE; a token requested in another browser is rejected.
Only in the online site's configuration file at the web host, outside the web folder – never on the PC, never in online storage, never in the history.
